subject: Averaging vectors with NA's in R

messages.author: 6a93cd2e837d2d7b
messages.subject: Averaging vectors with NA's in R
parts:
Simple data manipulation question:
I have two vectors, say:
c(1,3,NA,7,9) and
c(3,NA,7,9,11)
I'd like to return a vector of same length that is the mean of each respective vector position, and also ignore the NA's (so take the average of one number, not two). I don't want NA's in my answer unless the same position in each vector has an NA.

So, the answer I want is:
c(2,3,7,8,10)

Anyone have an elegant solution to this problem?
Thanks,
Jens

messages.author: 1ab3c88aacca70c5
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Averaging vectors with NA's in R
parts:
Jens,
I am relatively new to R, so this is not elegant at all.  But this will get you what you want:

q <- c(1,3,NA,7,9)
r <- c(3,NA,7,9,11)
mm <- matrix(c(q, r), , length(q), byrow = TRUE)
sapply(1:ncol(mm), function(i) mean(mm[ , i], na.rm=TRUE))

But there must be a less clunky way to do it.

Cheers,
Adam

messages.author: 6ed2ff7838c0c40e
messages.subject: Re: Averaging vectors with NA's in R
parts:
Jens,

The other two responses get the job done just fine, but just to add one more method to your arsenal, here's another way:

Assume your two vectors are called "a" and "b":

apply(cbind(a,b), 1, mean, na.rm=TRUE)

If you prefer to operate on a data frame, you can use basically the same approach:

df = data.frame(a,b)
apply(df, 1, mean, na.rm=TRUE)

The "1" tells the apply function to apply the mean function by row ("2" would be by column). The extra argument "na.rm=TRUE" gets passed by apply to the mean function.

You may run into situations where you want to nest one function within another, but you can't pass additional arguments. When that happens, you can just define a new function that passes those arguments. For example, if that were the case here, you could do the following:

new.mean = function(x) {mean(x, na.rm=TRUE)}
apply(cbind(a,b), 1, new.mean)

Hope that helps,
Joel
